question: does any recorded quantity separate the conditions, given that judged coverage does not
design: for each recorded per-episode quantity, the share of variance lying between condition means within a task, computed on the 15 admissible episodes
finding: process quantities separate the conditions sharply and artifact quantities separate them weakly, while judged coverage does not separate them at all. Interface calls give 0.899 and 0.951, context tokens 0.915 and 0.925, marginal tokens 0.845 and 0.896, and cost 0.771 and 0.936. Artifact size gives 0.367 and 0.702 and structural gap count 0.443 and 0.657. Judged coverage gives 0.009 and a clamped zero.
what_this_is_not: the process quantities are close to definitional. A condition that supplies more context and more interface access will make more calls and consume more tokens almost by construction, so a high share there is a manipulation check confirming the conditions differed in the intended way, and is not an effect on the quality of the work.
the_live_ambiguity: the manipulation demonstrably took effect, and the judged endpoint sees nothing. Either the conditions do not change artifact quality, or the endpoint cannot see the change. This design cannot distinguish those two readings, and the falsified retrieval filter and the near-zero condition component both sit on the second branch.
limits: one to two repeats per cell
shares computed within task then reported per task, not pooled
claim_scope: design diagnosis only; no treatment effect is claimed
